blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Embedding-level scaling expands the capacity of language models through lookup-based memory rather than by increasing model depth, width, or dense computation. Extending this idea to vision-language models (VLMs) is challenging because visual features are continuous, spatially structured, and query-dependent, unlike discrete text tokens that naturally support n-gram lookup. We introduce V-LUMEN, a visual lookup memory for VLMs. V-LUMEN discretizes visual features with a frozen codebook, builds spatially aware memory keys through spatial aggregation-based hashing, and modulates them with text-conditioned relevance signals; all addressing is non-parametric, and the retrieved embeddings are fused into the backbone through a gated residual pathway. On five reasoning-intensive benchmarks, V-LUMEN substantially improves a frozen Qwen3-VL-2B backbone and transfers zero-shot to three benchmarks whose images are disjoint from the training data. At a matched parameter budget, moving part of a LoRA or MoE adapter's capacity into V-LUMEN preserves accuracy on two backbones, indicating that external visual memory is an independent capacity axis rather than a stronger adaptation method. Because lookup cost is constant in table size and incurred only once at prefill, this capacity grows in storage rather than in per-token compute. Code is available at https://github.com/miso-choi/V-Lumen.
blocks.zh: 嵌入级的缩放通过基于取景的内存来扩展语言模型的能力,而不是通过增加模型的深度,宽度,或密集的计算来扩展. 将这个想法扩展至视觉语言模型(VLMs)具有挑战性,因为视觉特征是连续的,空间结构化的,并且依赖查询,与自然支持n克取景的离散文本符号不同. 我们介绍V -LUMEN, 一个视觉的查看记忆 VLMs。 V-LUMEN将可视特征用被冷冻的编码本进行盘片化,通过基于空间聚合的散列来构建空间意识内存键,并用文本条件的关联信号来调节;所有地址都是非参数化的,被取回的嵌入通过有门的剩余通道被熔接入骨干. 在五个推理密集型基准上,V-LUMEN大大改进了被冻结的Qune3-VL-2B主干线,并将零射入三个基准,其图像与培训数据脱节。 在相匹配的参数预算中,将LORA或MOE适配器的部分容量移入V-LUMEN上保留了两个主干线上的精度,表明外视内存是一个独立的容量轴而不是更强的适应方法. 因为表大小不变,而且只在预填时发生一次,所以这种容量在存储而不是每盘计算时会增长. 代码见https://github.com/miso-choi/V-Lumen。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Scaling vision–language models (VLMs) by widening or deepening the backbone pays a dense compute price at every forward pass. A natural question follows: can we grow a VLM’s visual representation capacity without growing its per-token compute?
blocks.zh: 放大视觉-语言模型(VLM), 一个自然的问题如下:我们能否在不增加VLM的直观表现能力的情况下,增加它的直观计算能力?

blocks.en: Recent work on LLMs answers an analogous question with external memory lookup . Engram Cheng et al. (2026) , STEM Sadhukhan et al. (2026) , and SCONE Yu et al. (2025) augment a language model with a large table of learned embeddings and address it through a non-parametric hash over token IDs, so capacity grows with the table size while per-token activated compute stays flat. These methods assume a discrete token alphabet. Visual features in a VLM are continuous, laid out on a 2-D patch grid, and their relevance depends on the question being asked, so a direct port of text-side lookup is not available.
blocks.zh: 最近关于LLMS的著作用外部内存检索解答了一个类似的问题。 Engram Cheng等人(2026年),STEM Sadhukhan等人(2026年),以及SCONE Yu等人. (2025年)用一个大型的学习嵌入表来增强语言模型,并通过一个非参数散列而不是代号ID来解决,因此能力随着表大小的增长而增长,而每盘激活的计算则保持平稳. 这些方法假设一个离散的符号字母表. VLM中的视觉特征是连续的,布置在二维补丁网格上,其相关性取决于被问到的问题,因此没有直接的文本端口搜索.

blocks.en: We introduce V-Lumen , an external visual memory for a VLM. V-Lumen is built from three components, each of which resolves one obstacle above. First, a frozen codebook Jin et al. (2024) discretizes continuous patch features into visual code IDs, giving the memory a stable, reusable address space. Second, Spatial Aggregation-based Hashing (SAH) folds row-, column-, and region-level context into the integer hash key, so the same code at different locations reaches different memory slots. Third, Text-Conditioned Hashing — via Projected Relevance Hashing (PRH) and its debiased variant Debiased Relevance Hashing (DRH) — modulates the key with a coarse text-to-visual relevance signal, so the same image patch can route to different memory slots under different questions. Retrieved memory cells are then fused into the backbone through Multi-Head Conditional Gating (MHCG), which assigns an independent gate per cell. All addressing on the memory side is non-parametric; only the memory tables and the fusion layer carry gradients.
blocks.zh: 我们介绍V-Lumen,一个VLM的外部视觉记忆. V-卢门由三个部分组成,每个部分解决上面的一个障碍. 第一,冷冻的密码本Jin et al. (2024)碟片将连续的补丁特性转化为视觉代码ID,使内存拥有稳定,可重复使用的地址空间. 第二,基于空间聚合的Hashing(SAH)将行,列,以及区域级的上下文折叠成整数散列键,因此不同位置的同一代码会达到不同的内存位. 第三,文本附加条件的Hashing——通过预测相关性Hashing(PRH)及其去偏差的变体 Dependent InternationalHashing(DRH)——用粗糙的文本对视觉相关性信号来调制密钥,因此同一图像补丁可以在不同的问题下通向不同的内存槽. 然后通过多头有条件的Gating(MHCG)将检索到的内存细胞连接到骨干中,每个细胞会分配一个独立的门. 内存一侧的所有地址都是非参数化的;只有内存表和聚变层带有梯度.

blocks.en: We evaluate V-Lumen on five reasoning-intensive vision-language benchmarks spanning chart, document, and multi-discipline understanding. Attached to a frozen Qwen3-VL-2B backbone, V-Lumen improves accuracy on all five benchmarks without updating any backbone weight, and it transfers zero-shot to three benchmarks whose images share no source with the training data. We then ask how this memory relates to adaptation methods that add capacity in other ways. At a matched total budget, combining a smaller LoRA or MoE adapter with V-Lumen performs on par with a larger adapter alone in Qwen3-VL-2B, and the MoE comparison carries over to a second backbone, InternVL3.5-2B. Part of an adapter’s capacity can thus be moved into an external memory without loss in accuracy, and this memory has a property that adapter parameters lack: its rows are addressed by hashing and only a few rows are read per visual token, rather than being used in dense matrix multiplications for every token. The memory can therefore, in principle, reside in host (CPU) memory or SSD-backed storage and be fetched on demand, as in large embedding tables of industrial recommendation models Naumov et al. (2019) ; Agarwal et al. (2023) ; Wilkening et al. (2021) and text-side lookup memories Cheng et al. (2026) , leaving GPU memory for the backbone and adapters. We therefore view V-Lumen as an independent capacity axis : capacity that matches adaptation in accuracy while growing in storage rather than in per-token compute.
blocks.zh: 我们评价V-Lumen的五个思维密集的视觉语言基准,这些基准跨越图表、文件和多学科理解。 V-Lumen附在被冻结的Qwen3-VL-2B主干线上,提高所有5个基准的精确度而不更新任何主干重量,它将零射入3个基准,其图像与训练数据没有共享源. 然后,我们询问这种记忆与以其他方式增加能力的适应方法有何关系。 在相应的总预算中,将一个较小的LORA或MOE适配器与V-Lumen在Qune3-VL-2B中单独与一个较大的适配器等效,而MOE的比较则延续到第二个主干,InternVL3.5-2B. 适配器的部分容量因此可以移动到外部内存中而不丧失准确性,而这个内存有适配器参数缺乏的属性:它的行通过散列处理,每个可视符只读几行,而不是用于每个符的密集矩阵乘法. 因此,原则上,记忆可以寄存在主机(CPU)存储器或SSD支撑存储器中,并按要求获取,例如工业推荐模型Naumov等人(2019年);Agarwal等人(2023年);Wilkening等人(2021年)和文本侧浏览记忆的大型嵌入表。 Cheng等人(2026年),将GPU内存留给骨干和适配器. 因此,我们认为V-Lumen是一个独立的能力轴:在储存中而不是每盘计算中,在精确度上匹配适应能力。

blocks.en: Our contributions are as follows. First, we extend lookup-based embedding scaling from discrete text tokens to continuous visual features, with a recipe in which every addressing mechanism is non-parametric: a frozen codebook for discrete addresses, spatial aggregation-based hashing for region-aware keys, and text-conditioned hashing for query-dependent keys. Second, we show that this visual memory forms an independent capacity axis. It improves a frozen backbone and transfers zero-shot to unseen image domains, and at the same total budget it matches LoRA and MoE adapters on two backbones while holding part of their capacity in an external memory rather than in adapter parameters. Third, we show that this capacity grows in storage rather than in per-token compute: lookup latency stays constant across a 40 × 40\times range of table sizes, and the memory adds a one-off prefill cost without changing per-token decode latency. Because the memory is addressed by hashing and read sparsely, it can in principle be served from host memory or storage, which we leave to future work.
blocks.zh: 我们的贡献如下。 首先,我们把基于仰视的嵌入式缩放从离散的文本符号扩展至连续的视觉特征,其中的食谱,每个地址机制都是非参数化的:一个用于离散地址的冻结代码簿,一个用于区域意识密钥的空间聚合式散列,以及用于依赖查询的密钥的文本条件散列。 第二,我们显示这种视觉记忆构成了一个独立的容量轴. 它改进了被冻结的主干线,并将零镜头传输到看不见的图像域,在同一总预算上,它与两个主干线上的LORA和MOE适配器匹配,同时在外部内存而不是适配器参数中持有部分容量. 第三,我们显示这种容量在存储中增长,而不是在每托肯计算中增长:在40×40\的表大小范围内,寻找时空保持恒定,内存增加了一次性的预填成本,而不改变每托肯解码时空. 由于记忆是通过散开和阅读稀疏的方式解决的,原则上可以从宿主记忆或存储服务,我们留给未来的工作.

blocks.en: 2 Method
blocks.zh: 2 方法

blocks.en: We briefly recall the Engram-style lookup memory that motivates the design of V-Lumen .
blocks.zh: 我们简短地回顾Engram风格的寻找记忆,

blocks.en:
Engram Cheng et al. (2026) augments language models with deterministic n n -gram lookup memory, where a fixed number of memory entries are retrieved per token and fused into the hidden state as a residual.
This scales accessible memory capacity without increasing the number of retrieved entries per token, providing a conditional-memory axis of sparse capacity, complementary to dense parameter scaling or MoE-style conditional computation.
blocks.zh:
Engram Cheng et al. (2026) 增加了语言模型,带有确定性 n -gram 检索内存,其中每个符件取回固定数量的内存条目,并熔化为隐藏状态的剩余部分.
这个缩放可访问的内存容量而不增加每个令牌检索的条目数量,提供一个容量稀少的有条件-记忆轴,是对密集参数缩放或MOE风格的有条件计算的补充.

blocks.en: 2.1 Overview
blocks.zh: 2.1 概览

blocks.en: Figure 1: Overview of V-Lumen . V-Lumen retrieves visual memory embeddings using spatially aggregated and text-conditioned hash keys, then fuses them into the frozen VLM through gated residual updates.
blocks.zh: 图1:V-Lumen概览 V-Lumen使用空间集成和文本条件的散列键检索视觉内存嵌入,然后通过闸门剩余更新将其熔化到冻结的VLM中.

blocks.en:
V-Lumen expands VLM capacity through a sparsely read external visual memory, a capacity axis that is independent of adaptation-based methods such as low-rank adapters and MoE-style conditional computation.
We retrieve per-position (visual token) embeddings from a memory, and conditionally fuse them back into the backbone hidden states via a residual pathway. V-Lumen specializes it to the vision side of a VLM through three components, as shown in Fig. 1 : (i) Visual Embedding Scaling (§ 2.2 ) discretizes continuous patch features into codebook indices and reads per-position memory vectors; (ii) Spatial Aggregation-based Hashing (§ 2.3 ) builds region-aware keys so that lookup uses local neighborhoods rather than isolated patches; and (iii) Text-Conditioned Hashing (§ 2.4 ) routes the same patch to query-adaptive memory slots, so that different text queries over the same image read from different parts of the memory. The retrieved memory is fused into the hidden states through a multi-head conditional gating (§ 2.5 ), and an optional small LoRA or MoE adapts the frozen backbone to the injected residual.

blocks.en: 2.2 Visual Embedding Scaling with External Memory
blocks.zh: 2.2 与外部内存嵌入的视觉放大

blocks.en:
A central challenge in visual embedding scaling is how to define reusable memory addresses for visual representations.
Unlike language tokens, which are already represented as discrete vocabulary indices, visual tokens are continuous feature vectors.
Directly using raw visual features as memory keys would lead to an overly sparse address space: even visually similar regions may produce slightly different features, making deterministic memory lookup unreliable and limiting memory reuse.
Moreover, storing memories for such fine-grained continuous addresses would be prohibitively inefficient.
We address this by introducing a discrete key space, where continuous visual features are mapped to compact code indices before memory lookup.
blocks.zh:
视觉嵌入缩放的一个中心挑战是如何定义可重复使用的内存地址,用于视觉表现.
与已经作为离散词汇索引表示的语言符号不同,视觉符号是连续的特征矢量.
直接使用原始视觉特征作为内存键会导致地址空间过于稀少:即使是视觉相似的区域也可能产生略微不同的特征,使得确定性内存的外观不可靠,并限制内存的再利用.
此外,为这种精细连续地址储存记忆效率低下,令人望而却步。
我们通过引入一个离散的密钥空间来解决这个问题,在这个空间中,连续的视觉特征在内存检索前被映射到紧凑的代码索引.

blocks.en: 2.3 Spatial Aggregation-based Hashing (SAH)

Visual memory keys should reflect not only which visual code appears at a patch, but also how that code is situated within the image.

blocks.en: 2.4 Text-Conditioned Hashing (TCH)
blocks.zh: 2.4 文字限制(TCH)

blocks.en: While image-only retrieval provides a fixed visual representation, the relevance of a specific region often depends on the input question. To account for this, we introduce Text-Conditioned Hashing (TCH), which makes the retrieval process query-aware. TCH modulates visual memory keys with text signals, allowing the same image region to point to different memory slots depending on the specific task or question.
blocks.zh: 虽然仅图像检索提供了固定的视觉表现,但特定区域的相关性往往取决于输入问题. 为此,我们引入了文本附加查询(TCH),这使得检索过程意识到查询。 TCH以文本信号调制视觉内存键,允许同一个图像区域根据特定的任务或问题指向不同的内存槽.

blocks.en:

(2022) , we apply it to query-conditioned visual memory indexing with two instantiations: Projected Relevance Hashing (PRH), described below, and its debiased variant Debiased Relevance Hashing (DRH); their exact forms and an ensemble are deferred to Appendix. blocks.en: Because rows are addressed by hashing, the cost of a lookup should not depend on the size of the memory table. We test this by scaling the number of rows per cell from 0.2 × 0.2\times to 8 × 8\times of our default setting (81,920 rows per cell, used in all main experiments), a 40 × 40\times range, while keeping all other components fixed (Tab. 1 ). A lookup consists of two stages. Key construction computes row indices from the spatially aggregated codes, coordinate bins, text-conditioned bins, and per-cell hashing, without accessing the table. Gather then reads the memory embeddings at those indices. We measure both stages for one fusion layer with 64 visual tokens in bf16 on a single RTX 6000 Ada GPU, averaging 50 runs after 10 warm-up runs.

blocks.en: 3.1 Experimental Settings
blocks.zh: 3.1 实验设置

blocks.en:
The strategic design of our training data is paramount to ensuring that the visual memory captures reusable visual priors rather than merely memorizing task-specific answers. To facilitate this, we deliberately curate a training corpus from diverse domains characterized by high visual pattern recurrence, such as document layouts, tabular structures, and OCR regions.
This exposes the model to similar visual motifs across varied contexts, providing training signals that can make memory lookup beneficial for downstream reasoning tasks.
blocks.zh:
我们培训数据的战略设计对于确保视觉内存能够捕捉可重复使用的视觉前科,而不仅仅是记忆特定任务的答案至关重要。 为了促进这一点,我们有意从各种领域,如文件布局、表格结构以及OCR区域,对具有高视觉模式重现特征的培训材料进行整理。
这让模型在不同的背景中暴露出类似的视觉动机,提供能够使内存外观有利于下游推理任务的训练信号.

blocks.en: The training consists of two stages with different data mixtures: mid-training and SFT. The goal of mid-training is to form visual static priors in the memory, while the goal of SFT is reasoning alignment after memory retrieval.
blocks.zh: 培训包括两个阶段,有不同的数据混合物:中级培训和SFT。 中训的目标是在内存中形成视觉静态前缀,而SFT的目标是在内存检索后进行推理对齐.

blocks.en: In the mid-training stage, we organize the data into four groups to help the model learn various visual patterns. The first group focuses on documents and charts, using DocVQA Mathew et al. (2021) , ChartQA Masry et al. (2022) , InfographicVQA Mathew et al. (2022) , and ScienceQA Lu et al. (2022) to learn recurring layouts such as tables, grids, and text structures. The second group includes spatial-structure data, Visual Genome Krishna et al. (2017) , GQA Hudson and Manning (2019) , and RefCOCO/RefCOCOg Yu et al. (2016) , which help the model understand how objects relate to each other. The remaining groups consist of diagrams from AI2D Kembhavi et al. (2016) and natural scenes from AOKVQA Schwenk et al. (2022) and TextCaps Sidorov et al. (2020) . For ScienceQA during this stage, we use a special method where the model predicts the lecture explanation before the answer. This helps the model connect its visual memory with the underlying meaning of the image.
blocks.zh: 在中训阶段,我们将数据组织成四组,以帮助模型学习各种视觉模式. 第一组侧重于文件和图表,使用DocVQA Mathew等人(2021年), ChartQA。 Masry等人(2022年),InfographyVQA Mathew等人(2022年),以及ScienceQA Lu等人(2022年)学习表,网格,文本结构等反复出现的布局. 第二组包括空间结构数据、Visual Genome Krishna等人(2017年)、GQA Hudson和Manning(2019年)和RefCO/RefCOg。 Yu et al. (2016),帮助模型了解物体之间如何相互关联. 其余各组由AI2D Kembhavi等人(2016年)的图和AOKVQA Schwenk等人(2022年)和TextCaps Sidorov等人(2020年)的自然场景组成. 科学 在这个阶段,我们使用一种特殊的方法,即模型在回答前预测讲座解释. 这有助于模型将其视觉记忆与图像的基本含义联系起来.

blocks.en: During SFT, we use datasets that require high-level thinking, including ScienceQA, AI2D, DocVQA, ChartQA, GQA, and AOKVQA, to teach the model how to use retrieved information correctly. During this stage, we no longer use the lecture explanation policy and instead train the model to predict the final answer directly. This process ensures the model can use its memory to support deeper reasoning and generate accurate responses for complex tasks.
blocks.zh: 在SFT期间,我们使用需要高层次思考的数据集,包括ScienceQA,AI2D,DocVQA,ChartQA,GQA,以及AOKVQA,来教导模型如何正确使用检索到的信息. 在这个阶段,我们不再使用讲座解释政策,而是训练模型直接预测最终答案. 这个过程确保了模型能够利用其内存支持更深入的推理,并产生对复杂任务的准确的响应.

blocks.en: For evaluation-domain adaptation, we additionally use 10 % \% of each evaluation dataset as few-shot training data and reserve the remaining 90 % \% strictly for evaluation.
blocks.zh: 在评价领域适应方面,我们还将每套评价数据集的10%作为少见的培训数据,并将其余90%严格用于评价。

We evaluated V-Lumen on five vision–language benchmarks that emphasize reasoning: ChartMuseum Tang et al. (2025) , FRIEDA Pyo et al. (2026) , VisRes Törtei et al. (2025) , MMMU Yue et al. (2024) , and MMMU-Pro Yue et al. (2025) .
For consistency with our few-shot protocol, evaluation used the held-out 90% partition induced by the fixed split seed, from which we sampled up to 1,000 examples for each benchmark.
We report relaxed accuracy: for numeric answers we accept predictions within 5% relative error of the ground truth when both can be parsed as numbers; otherwise we compare predictions to answers after light normalization (case, punctuation, whitespace).

我们报告放松的准确性:对于数值答案,当两者都可以被解析为数字时,我们接受地面真理相对误差5%范围内的预测;否则,我们将预测与光常化后的答案进行比较(案例,圆点,白空间).

blocks.en:
V-Lumen is trained in two stages.
In both stages, we update only the trainable paths of each configuration, including LoRA/MoE weights and/or V-Lumen memory tables and fusion parameters, while keeping the backbone f θ f_{\theta} frozen.
The training objective is next-token cross-entropy with an answer-only mask, where image and prompt tokens do not contribute to the loss.
For V-Lumen +LoRA/MoE, the adaptation modules and V-Lumen fusion parameters are fine-tuned jointly.
Both stages use AdamW ( β = ( 0.9 , 0.95 ) \beta{=}(0.9,0.95) , weight decay 0.01 0.01 ), bf16 mixed precision, a cosine learning-rate schedule with a 200 200 -step linear warmup, and gradient clipping at global norm 1.0 1.0 . For additional implementation details, please refer to Appendix. E .

blocks.en: 3.2 Experimental Results
blocks.zh: 3.2 实验结果

blocks.en:
Tab. 2 reports results on five reasoning-intensive vision-language benchmarks, using Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct Bai et al. (2025) as the backbone for all experiments. The table consists of three comparison blocks.
(i) The vanilla-based block attaches V-Lumen to the frozen backbone and asks whether a visual lookup memory alone improves reasoning.
(ii) The LoRA-based block compares LoRA + V-Lumen , which combines LoRA( k k ) with V-Lumen (1), against LoRA-only, a larger LoRA( 1 + k 1{+}k ) adapter scaled to the same total trainable-parameter budget . The two differ in how this budget is used at inference: in LoRA-only, every added parameter is activated in each token’s forward pass, whereas in LoRA + V-Lumen , only the LoRA component is fully activated and the memory contributes just the few rows retrieved for each visual token.
(iii) The MoE-based block compares MoE + V-Lumen , which combines MoE( k k ) with V-Lumen (1), against MoE-only, a larger MoE( 1 + k 1{+}k ) matched in both accessible parameters (all parameters the model can route to) and activated parameters per token. Both sides are sparse: MoE-only activates the routed expert for each token, while MoE + V-Lumen activates a smaller routed expert together with the retrieved memory rows.
blocks.zh:
Tab. 2报告以Qune3-VL-2B-Instruct Bai et al. (2025)作为所有实验的骨干,得出了五个推理密集型视觉语言基准的结果。 该表由三个比较区块组成.
(一) 以香草为主的块将V-Lumen附在冰冻的骨干上,并询问仅一个视觉的仰视内存是否会改善推理.
(二)基于LORA的区块将LORA + V-Lumen → 将LORA(k k)与V-Lumen (1)合并,仅限LORA → 更大的LORA(1 + k 1{+}k)适配器缩放到相同的总可列车参数预算. 两者在推论中如何使用预算有所不同:在仅LORA语中,每个添加的参数都会被激活在每个令牌的前传中,而在LORA + V-Lumen语中,只有LORA语部分被完全激活,内存只为每个视觉令牌检索到的几行.
(三)基于MOE的区块比较MOE + V-Lumen → 该区块将MOE(k k)与V-Lumen (1)结合,只对应MOE,一个更大的MOE(1 + k 1{+}k),匹配两个可访问参数(所有该模型可路径到的参数)和每个令牌的激活参数. 双方都是稀疏的:只使用MOE激活每个符的路由专家,而MoE + V-Lumen则激活一个较小的路由专家与被检索的内存行.

blocks.en: Frozen backbone. Attaching V-Lumen to the frozen vanilla backbone improves accuracy by + 17.79 ± 0.47 +17.79\pm 0.47 pp on average, with gains on all five benchmarks. Without updating any backbone weight, adding a visual lookup memory alone substantially strengthens visual reasoning. This setting uses a longer training schedule than the adapter-based settings (Appendix E.2 ), so we do not compare it directly against LoRA-only or MoE-only.
blocks.zh: 冻骨骨. 将V-Lumen附在冷冻的香草骨干上能提高精度,平均为+17.79±0.47+17.79\pm0.47pp,所有五个基准都有增益. 在不更新任何骨干重量的情况下,仅添加一个视觉外观记忆就大大加强了视觉推理. 此设置使用比基于适配器的设置(Appendix E.2 )更长的训练时间表,因此我们不直接将其与仅限LORA或只限MOE比较.

blocks.en:
Matched budgets. When part of the budget is reallocated from adapter parameters to V-Lumen , performance is preserved. In the MoE-based block, MoE + V-Lumen reaches + 16.92 ± 0.91 +16.92\pm 0.91 pp versus + 16.85 ± 0.95 +16.85\pm 0.95 pp for MoE-only, with higher accuracy on ChartMuseum and VisRes and lower accuracy on the other three benchmarks. In the LoRA-based block, LoRA + V-Lumen reaches +21.15 ± \pm 0.02pp versus
+20.58 ± \pm 0.85pp for LoRA-only (+0.57pp), higher on MMMU-Pro and ChartMuseum,
on par on FRIEDA and MMMU, and lower on VisRes. Both differences are within about
one seed standard deviation of the adapter-only baseline, so we do not claim that
lookup memory improves over adaptation at a fixed budget. blocks.en:
We use a 10% few-shot / 90% evaluation protocol on the benchmarks in Tab. 2 . These benchmarks are recent and highly challenging, and the 2B backbone scores near zero without in-domain adaptation, so a small few-shot split is needed to obtain a measurable signal.
To evaluate V-Lumen without any in-domain adaptation, we further test it in a fully zero-shot setting on three benchmarks outside our training curriculum, comparing the frozen Qwen3-VL-2B backbone with V-Lumen disabled and enabled on 1,000 samples per benchmark (Tab. 3 ).
None of the three benchmarks shares image sources with our training data (Appendix F ), and no in-domain few-shot samples are used. V-Lumen improves over the frozen backbone on all three benchmarks and in every seed, spanning three independently sourced image domains. This suggests that the retrieved memory encodes reusable visual priors rather than memorizing the training distribution.

No probe parameters are trained. Text-only Engram Cheng et al. (2026) reports that lookup memory lets intermediate layers approach the final prediction earlier, which it interprets as accelerated convergence; we test whether visual memory behaves similarly.

blocks.en: We probe the main-table checkpoints (fusion layers (2, 8)), using the same inputs and evaluation samples as the main evaluation. For MoE, we use the budget-matched pair of Tab. 2 . For LoRA, we use the rank-matched pair of Tab. 5 (LoRA(0.5) with and without V-Lumen ), whose adapter is identical on both sides, so that layer-wise differences isolate the effect of the memory. Among the four (adapter, benchmark) pairs in which adding V-Lumen improves over the corresponding adapter-only model, we analyze the two whose answers are a single option letter, VisRes (MoE) and MMMU-Pro (LoRA), for which the layer-wise top-1 accuracy of the gold answer is well defined. Since these pairs are selected because V-Lumen improves on them, they are not a random sample of benchmarks. All results are means over three seeds (Fig. 2 ).

blocks.en: Up to layer 18, neither model ranks the gold answer first and the JSD stays at its maximum ( ln ⁡ 2 \ln 2 ) on both benchmarks, so the probes can distinguish the two models only from layer 19 onward. There, the V-Lumen models tend to approach their final prediction earlier. Averaged over layers 19–26, the JSD to the final prediction is lower with V-Lumen on both benchmarks ( − 0.036 -0.036 on VisRes and − 0.004 -0.004 on MMMU-Pro), and on VisRes the gold answer becomes the top-1 prediction earlier, with leads of + 7.4 +7.4 and + 4.4 +4.4 points at layers 19 and 20 in two of three seeds. At the final layer, top-1 accuracy rises from 0.236 to 0.251 on VisRes and from 0.277 to 0.289 on MMMU-Pro, matching the margins in Tab. 2 . This pattern is consistent with the accelerated convergence reported for Engram. However, the differences are small relative to seed variance: in each pair, only two of three seeds show a lower JSD, and the mean difference lies within one standard deviation across seeds. We therefore read these probes as a tendency rather than a consistent effect, in line with the modest accuracy margins in Tab. 2 .

blocks.zh: 5 相关工作

blocks.en: 5.1 Embedding Scaling in LLMs
blocks.zh: 5.1 在法学硕士课程中嵌入扩展

blocks.en: Embedding-level scaling has emerged as an axis of model capacity that is complementary to scaling depth, width, or dense computation. Lookup-based methods expand accessible capacity through sparsely accessed embedding memories: Engram Cheng et al. (2026) retrieves static n n -gram memories through deterministic lookup and fuses them into the hidden state, and STEM Sadhukhan et al. (2026) replaces FFN up-projections with layer-local embedding lookup, decoupling capacity growth from per-token dense computation. A related line scales token or n n -gram representations themselves: N-Grammer Roy et al. (2022) augments transformers with latent n n -gram embeddings built from discrete token representations, SCONE Yu et al. (2025) learns contextualized embeddings for frequent n n -grams with a separate transformer, and vocabulary scaling studies show that larger or compute-optimal vocabularies improve language modeling efficiency and performance Huang et al. (2025) ; Tao et al. (2024) .
blocks.zh: 嵌入级的缩放已成为模型能力的轴线,是对缩放深度,宽度或密集计算的补充. 基于搜索的方法通过很少访问的嵌入记忆来扩展访问能力: 语句 程等编. (2026年)通过确定性的检查来回收静态n-gram记忆,并将它们导入隐藏状态,以及STEM Sadhukhan等人. (2026)用层-局部嵌入式仰视取代FFN上投影,将容量增长与每盘密集计算脱钩. 相关的线性比例符或n-gm表示本身: N-Grammer Roy 等人. blocks.en: Several of these designs also exploit the fact that embedding tables need not reside in accelerator memory. SCONE precomputes its embeddings into an off-accelerator store, MoLE Jie et al. (2025) reparameterizes expert computation as lookup tables for inference, and the per-layer embeddings of Gemma 3n Google DeepMind (2024) can be generated outside the model’s operating memory and cached for layer-wise execution. Together, these works treat embedding tables as a capacity reservoir that grows in storage rather than in per-token compute.
blocks.zh: 其中一些设计还利用了嵌入式表格不必放在加速器内存这一事实。 SCONE将其嵌入到一个离加速器商店,MoLE Jie等人. (2025)重新将专家计算作为推论的查询表,每层Gemma 3n Google DeepMind的嵌入(2024)可以在模型的操作内存之外生成,并缓存用于层层执行. 这些工程将嵌入式表视为储存中而不是每盘计算中生长的能力库。

blocks.en: All of these methods, however, rely on the discreteness of language tokens, which naturally supports vocabulary expansion, n n -gram indexing, and deterministic lookup. Visual features in VLMs are instead continuous, spatially structured, and query-dependent, so text-based embedding scaling does not transfer directly. V-Lumen extends lookup-based scaling to this setting by discretizing continuous visual features and constructing spatially aware and text-conditioned memory keys. Related work on spatial aggregation is discussed in Appendix. C .
blocks.zh: 然而,所有这些方法都依赖于语言符号的离散性,语言符号自然支持词汇扩展,n-gram索引化,以及决定性的查找. VLMs中的视觉特征相反是连续的,空间结构的,并且依赖查询,因此基于文本的嵌入缩放不会直接传输. V-Lumen通过将连续的视觉特征盘片化,构建空间意识和文本条件的内存密钥,将基于仰视的缩放扩展至此设置. 关于空间汇总的相关工作在附录中讨论。 丙 .

blocks.en: 5.2 Hash-based and Deterministic Routing
blocks.zh: 5.2 以大麻为主和有决定性的路线

blocks.en: Sparse-MoE architectures route inputs via a learned gate, but the learned router is notoriously unstable: load-imbalance collapse and auxiliary balancing losses are documented in Switch Transformer Fedus et al. (2022) . A parallel line replaces the learned router with a non-parametric function: Hash Layers Roller et al. (2021) (fixed hash), BASE Layers Lewis et al. (2021) (balanced assignment as a linear program), and THOR Zuo et al. (2022) (stochastic expert selection). Our TCH (§ 2.4 ) transposes this pattern from expert selection to memory addressing: the same patch under different queries is routed to different slots of one memory bank via a frozen random projection and a rank-bucket XOR.
blocks.zh: Sparse-MoE架构通过学习门输入路由,但学习路由器却臭名昭著地不稳定:负载-平衡崩溃和辅助平衡损失在Switch Transformer Fedus等人(2022)中都有记载. 一条平行线用非参数函数取代已学习的路由器: Hash Lails Roller等人(2021年)(固定散列),BASE Lailes Lewis等人(2021年)(平衡分配为线性程序),THOR Zuo等人(2022年)(史诗专家选拔). 我们的TCH(§ 2.4)将这个模式从专家选择转换为内存地址:不同查询下的同一补丁通过冻结的随机投影和排行XOR,被路由到一个内存库的不同插槽.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: We introduced V-Lumen , an external visual lookup memory for vision-language models. Three components make lookup-based scaling work on the vision side: a frozen codebook that maps continuous patch features to discrete codes that serve as memory addresses (§ 2.2 ), non-parametric spatial aggregation that turns isolated patch codes into region-aware keys (§ 2.3 ), and text-conditioned hashing that routes the same patch to different memory slots depending on the query (§ 2.4 ). V-Lumen improves a frozen backbone and transfers zero-shot to unseen image domains. At the same total budget, it matches LoRA and MoE adapters while holding part of their capacity in an external memory rather than in adapter parameters, forming an independent capacity axis whose capacity grows in storage rather than in per-token compute. Because this memory is addressed by hashing and read sparsely, it opens a path toward serving visual capacity outside GPU memory.
blocks.zh: 我们引入了V-Lumen, 视觉语言模型的外部视觉搜索内存。 三个组件在视觉方面进行基于外观的缩放工作:将连续补丁特征映射到作为内存地址的离散代码(§ 2.2)的冷冻编码本,将孤立的补丁代码转换成区域感知键的非参数空间聚合(§ 2.3),以及根据查询情况将同一补丁路径到不同内存槽的文字条件散列(§ 2.4). V-Lumen改进冷冻骨干,将零镜头传输到看不见的图像域. 在同一总预算中,它与LORA和MOE适配器匹配,同时在外部内存而不是适配器参数中持有部分容量,形成独立的容量轴,其容量在存储中而不是在每托肯计算中增长. 由于这种记忆是通过散列和阅读稀疏的方式解决的,它打开了一条在GPU记忆之外服务视觉能力的路径.

blocks.zh: 7 未来工作

blocks.en: Each visual token reads only | O | ⋅ H |O|\cdot H rows of the memory table (Eq. ( 9 )), and these rows are addressed by hashing rather than used in dense matrix multiplications. The table can therefore, in principle, reside in host (CPU) memory or SSD-backed storage and be fetched on demand, as in the large embedding tables of industrial recommendation models Naumov et al. (2019) ; Agarwal et al. (2023) ; Wilkening et al. (2021) and text-side lookup memories Cheng et al. (2026) . Unlike text-side memories, whose addresses depend only on input token IDs, the addresses of V-Lumen are computed from hidden states at the first fusion layer, so fetching for later fusion layers can overlap with computation but fetching for the first cannot. Measuring the latency and throughput of such a deployment, and designing prefetching policies around this constraint, is a natural next step.

blocks.en: Key construction accounts for about three quarters of the prefill overhead in our implementation (Appendix H.1 ). It consists of integer hashing and indexing over the visual-token grid, so vectorizing it on the GPU while keeping the computed addresses identical should remove most of this overhead.
blocks.zh: 关键建筑占我们执行中预填间接费用的约四分之三(附录H.1 )。 它包括整数散列和在视觉磁盘网格上的索引,因此在GPU上矢量化,同时保持计算地址的完全相同,应当去除大部分的这种间接费用.

blocks.en: Additional rows are free in per-token compute but do not yet improve accuracy in our setting, whereas wider memory vectors do (Appendix J ). Understanding what the memory learns, and how training data and key design affect how much of a larger table is used, could let the row axis deliver the gains that width currently provides without increasing the per-token read.

blocks.en: Extending V-Lumen to backbones beyond 2B parameters would test whether the capacity axis persists with scale. The component ablation (Appendix I.4 ) also suggests evaluating settings where visual codes shift systematically, such as reusing a trained memory after the vision encoder or connector is updated.

blocks.en: Appendix A Limitations
blocks.zh: 附录A

blocks.en: At a matched parameter budget, V-Lumen matches LoRA and MoE adapters in accuracy, so the advantage of holding capacity in an external memory lies in system-level properties that we have argued from its design but not yet fully demonstrated. First, because the memory is addressed by hashing and only a few rows are read per visual token, it can in principle be served from host memory or storage rather than GPU memory. We have not measured such a deployment: in our implementation, the memory table resides in GPU memory in fp32, and the prefill overhead (19–25 ms; Appendix H.1 ) is dominated by key construction computed with a Python loop on the CPU, so the reported latency reflects our implementation rather than a lower bound. Second, the number of memory rows can grow without increasing per-token compute, as lookup latency stays constant across a 40 × 40\times range of table sizes (Tab. 1 ). In our current setting, however, additional rows have not yet translated into higher accuracy, whereas widening the retrieved vectors does improve accuracy while slightly increasing the per-token read (Appendix J ). This suggests that the training data and key design, rather than table size, currently bound how much of the memory is used, which leaves room for improving how a larger table is filled and read. Turning these properties into measured benefits is the main direction for future work (§ 7 ).
blocks.zh: 在匹配的参数预算中,V-Lumen在精确度上与LORA和MOE适配器匹配,因此在外部内存中持有容量的优势在于我们从它的设计中论证但尚未充分展示的系统级属性. 首先,由于内存通过散列处理,并且每个视觉符号只读到几行,因此原则上可以从主机内存或存储器而不是GPU内存中服务. 我们没有衡量这样的部署:在我们的执行中,内存表存在于fp32的GPU内存中,预填高空(19–25 ms;附录H.1)则以使用CPU上的Python环计算的关键构造为主,因此所报道的缓存反映了我们的执行而不是较低的约束. 第二,内存行数可以在不增加每个托肯计算数的情况下增长,因为检索时空在表大小的40×40\时间范围内保持不变(Tab. 1 ). 然而,在我们目前的设置中,额外的行尚未转化为更高的准确性,而扩大检索的矢量确实提高了准确性,同时略微提高了每盘读数(附录J )。 这表明培训数据和关键设计,而不是表格大小,目前约束了内存的使用量,这为改进更大表的填充和阅读方式留有余地. 将这些属性转化为衡量效益是未来工作的主要方向(第7节)。

blocks.en: Appendix B Broader Impact
blocks.zh: 附录B

blocks.en: V-Lumen adds capacity to a vision-language model through an external memory that is addressed by hashing and read only a few rows at a time, rather than through parameters used in every forward pass. If this memory is served from slower but larger memory tiers, such as host memory on a server or flash storage on a device, capacity could be added to VLMs deployed under tight accelerator-memory budgets, including on-device and edge settings, without a matching increase in accelerator memory or per-token compute. Related designs in language models already keep embedding tables outside the accelerator’s working memory Google DeepMind (2024) ; Cheng et al. (2026) . Such deployments could lower the hardware cost and energy of running capable multimodal models and make them available on consumer hardware and in settings with limited connectivity, where processing images locally can also keep user data on the device. We have not yet measured such deployments (Appendix A ), so these benefits remain potential.
blocks.zh: V-Lumen通过一个通过散列处理,一次只读几行的外部内存,而不是通过每个前传中使用的参数,为视觉语言模型增加容量. 如果这种内存服务于较慢但较大的内存级,如服务器上的主机内存或设备上的闪存,可以在紧凑的加速器-记忆预算下,包括安装上和边缘设置下,将容量添加到部署在VLM上,而无需匹配加速器内存或每托肯计算. 语言模型中的相关设计已经在加速器的工作内存Google DeepMind(2024)之外保留了嵌入表; 程等 (2026) (中文(简体) ). 这种部署可以降低运行有能力的多式联运模型的硬件成本和能量,并在消费者硬件上和连接有限的情况下提供,在当地处理图像也可以保存设备上的用户数据。 我们尚未衡量这种部署(附录A),因此这些好处仍然是潜在的。

blocks.en: At the same time, making capable VLMs easier to deploy broadly also lowers the barrier to misuse, for example in surveillance or automated decision-making without human oversight, and carries over the risks of the underlying backbone, including incorrect or overconfident predictions and biases inherited from pretrained models and training data. Because the memory table stores content learned from training images, models trained on sensitive data could retain information from that data. Our work does not introduce new datasets of sensitive content or a deployed system, and any practical use should follow the safety, fairness, and privacy requirements of the target application and include human oversight where errors could have significant consequences.
blocks.zh: 同时,使有能力的甚高频更便于广泛部署,也降低了滥用的障碍,例如在没有人类监督的监视或自动决策方面,并承担了基础骨干的风险,包括不正确或过度自信的预测以及从预先培训的模型和培训数据中继承的偏见。 由于内存表存储了从培训图像中学习到的内容,在敏感数据方面接受培训的模型可以保留该数据中的信息. 我们的工作没有引入敏感内容的新数据集或部署的系统,任何实际使用都应遵循目标应用的安全性,公正性和隐私性要求,并在错误可能产生严重后果时包括人的监督.

blocks.en: Our spatial aggregation design (§ 2.3 ) draws on prior work that uses axis-aligned operations for efficient spatial context modeling, including strip pooling Hou et al. blocks.en: D.5 Distinction from Cross-Modal Query Bridges
blocks.zh: D.5 与跨莫达尔查询桥的区别

blocks.en:
Prior VLMs often use trainable query or bridge modules to connect visual encoders with language models, such as Perceiver-style latent arrays Jaegle et al. (2022) , Flamingo’s Perceiver Resampler and gated cross-attention Alayrac et al. (2022) , and the Q-Former modules in BLIP-2 Li et al. (2023) and InstructBLIP Dai et al. (2023) .
Although these methods also introduce text- or query-dependent visual processing, their role is fundamentally different from our text-conditioned hashing.
Bridge modules learn to transform, compress, or select visual features so that they can be consumed by the language model.
In contrast, V-Lumen keeps the backbone interface unchanged and uses text-conditioned signals only to alter the memory addressing process for external visual memory lookup.
blocks.zh:
先前的VLM常使用可训练查询或桥模块将视觉编码器与语言模型连接起来,如Perceiver风格的潜在阵列Jaegle等人(2022年),Flamingo的Perceiver Resampler和Gated cross-attention Alayrac等人(2022年),以及BLIP-2 Li等人(2023年)和InstructBLIP Dai等人(2023年)中的Q-Former模块.
虽然这些方法也引入了文本依赖或查询依赖的视觉处理,但是它们的作用与我们的文本条件散列完全不同.
桥梁模块学习转换,压缩,或选择视觉特征,以便被语言模型所消耗.
相比之下,V-Lumen保持主干接口不变,使用文字条件信号只是为了改变外部视觉内存检索的内存地址进程.

blocks.en:
Therefore, our method should not be interpreted as another cross-modal connector.
The projected relevance hashing component uses a frozen random projection and similarity-based scoring, rather than a learned query module or soft cross-attention.
Its goal is not to produce language-aligned visual tokens, but to make the memory address depend on the input instruction.
This provides a lightweight distinction from query-bridge architectures: they learn how to read visual features into the language model, whereas V-Lumen determines which reusable memory embeddings are retrieved for a given visual pattern and text query.
blocks.zh:
因此,我们的方法不应被解释为另一个跨模式连接器。
预测的相关散列组件使用冷冻随机投影和基于相似性的评分,而不是学习的查询模块或柔软的交叉注意.
其目标不是制作语言相通的视觉符号,而是使内存地址取决于输入指令.
这提供了与查询-桥架构的轻量级区分:他们学会了如何将视觉特征读入语言模型,而V-Lumen则决定了哪些可重用内存嵌入器被检索到某个特定的视觉模式和文本查询.

blocks.en: Zero-shot claims are most often questioned on image exposure rather than annotation leakage. For each of the three zero-shot benchmarks in Tab. 3 , the QA pairs are distinct from our training annotations, and we additionally verify that the benchmark shares no images with our training corpus.

blocks.en: We evaluate on the TextVQA Singh et al. (2019) validation split, whose images are drawn from Open Images Kuznetsova et al. (2020) . One of our training sources, TextCaps Sidorov et al. (2020) , reuses TextVQA images and follows the same train/val partition, and we train only on the TextCaps train split. The two sets are therefore disjoint by construction. We further confirm this with an image-ID check, finding that no TextVQA validation image appears in our training data.
blocks.zh: 我们评价TextVQA Singh等人(2019年)验证分裂,其图像来自Open Images Kuznetsova等人(2020年). 我们的训练来源之一,TextCaps Sidorov et al. (2020年),再利用TextVQA图像,并遵循相同的列车/val分区,我们只在TextCaps列车拆分上进行训练. 因此,这两套方案因施工而脱节。 我们通过图像识别检查进一步确认这一点,发现我们的培训数据中没有文本VQA验证图像。

blocks.en: VizWiz-VQA Gurari et al. (2018) consists of photos taken by blind and low-vision users through the VizWiz mobile app. OCR-VQA Mishra et al. (2019) consists of book-cover images collected from an online bookstore. Neither collection pipeline draws on COCO, Visual Genome, or Open Images, which underlie our natural-image training sources. Neither draws on our document, chart, or diagram sources either. Both benchmarks are therefore disjoint from our training images at the source level, and no image-ID audit is required.
blocks.zh: 维兹维兹-VQA Gurari et al. (2018)由盲人和低视用户通过VizWiz移动应用拍摄的照片组成. OCR-VQA Mishra et al. (2019)由从一个在线书店收集的图书封面图像组成. 无论是COCO、Visual Genome还是Open Images, 既不利用我们的文档、图表,也不利用图表来源。 因此,这两项基准都与我们在来源一级的培训图像脱节,不需要进行图像识别审计。

blocks.en: Tab. 12 reports GPU memory after loading each model and the peak during inference (same checkpoints and hardware as Tab. 10 ). When V-Lumen is added on top of the vanilla backbone or LoRA(0.5), GPU memory increases by 0.35 GB. Almost all of this is the memory table: our implementation keeps all trainable modules, including the memory table, LoRA adapters, and MoE experts, in fp32 on top of the bf16 backbone, so the table’s 83,952,896 parameters occupy 0.34 GB. At a matched total budget, the increase nearly vanishes: 0.003 GB for the LoRA pair (LoRA(1.5) → \rightarrow LoRA(0.5) + V-Lumen , 4.772 → \rightarrow 4.775 GB; 0.001 GB at peak) and 0.02 GB for the MoE pair (4.781 → \rightarrow 4.801 GB, with the same increase at peak). In both cases, the adapter component of the + V-Lumen variant is smaller than the adapter-only baseline (LoRA rank 107 vs. 321; 21 experts of width 168 vs. 31 of width 344), which offsets nearly all of the table’s footprint; at a matched budget, V-Lumen reallocates memory rather than adding to it. In our current implementation, the memory table resides on the GPU; offloading it to host memory is left to future work.

blocks.en: The salts, prime multipliers, and rolling-hash coefficients used in V-Lumen (Appendix D.3 ) are not tuned hyperparameters. They only serve to give different addressing components (coordinates, text-conditioned bins, and n n -gram orders) distinct, non-colliding contributions to the hash key, following standard hashing practice. blocks.en: This difference between key designs appears only under the stress test. Under common image degradation such as JPEG compression and downscaling, which also change most of the visual codes, all variants, including rolling hash only, remain robust, with accuracy changes below 1pp. A re-drawn projection is harsher because it assigns new codes at random, including to informative patches. Spatial aggregation and text-conditioned hashing may therefore matter in settings where codes shift more systematically than under natural degradation, for example when a trained memory is reused after the vision encoder or connector is updated, or under small adversarial perturbations of the input; we do not evaluate these settings here.
blocks.zh: 关键设计之间的这种差异仅在压力测试下出现. 在JPEG压缩和降尺度等常见图像降解下,也改变大部分视觉码,所有变体,包括仅滚动散列,都保持稳健,精度变化低于1pp. 重新绘制的投影更严酷,因为它随机分配新的代码,包括信息补丁. 因此,空间聚合和文本条件的散列在编码比自然退化下更系统化的环境下可能很重要,例如,在视觉编码器或连接器更新后,经过训练的内存被重新使用,或者输入受到小的对抗性干扰;我们不评估这些设置。

blocks.en: We hypothesize that the full design degrades less under the stress test because of row sharing , rather than because its addresses survive the perturbation or because it relies less on the memory. Spatial aggregation blends each code with its row- and column-wise context before hashing, and text-conditioned hashing further salts the key with the query, so each memory row is reached by many codes and contexts during training and learns more generic content. Reading a row trained for a different code therefore costs little. Rolling-hash keys, in contrast, map nearly one-to-one to code n n -grams, so their rows are specific to particular code sequences and reading a wrong row injects noise. The two alternative explanations do not hold: when all codes change, every memory address changes for all key designs, and the average fusion-gate activation is similar across designs (0.61–0.67). We have not verified this hypothesis directly, and the stress test uses a single draw of the perturbed projection.
blocks.zh: 我们假设整个设计在压力测试下 的降解较少 因为排位共享, 而不是因为它的地址 在扰动中幸存 或因为它较少依赖内存。 空间聚合在散开前将每个代码与其行和列的上下文混合在一起,而文字条件化的散开则将键与查询的更多盐分混合在一起,因此每个内存行在训练期间被许多代码和上下文所达到,并学习了更通用的内容. 因此,阅读为不同代码而训练的一行文件的费用很少。 滚动-hash键,相对而言,将近1对1映射到编码n-gram,因此他们的行是特定代码序列的特异性,读错一行注入噪音. 两种备选解释并不坚持:当所有代码改变时,所有关键设计的每一个内存地址都改变,平均聚变门激活在各种设计上是相似的(0.61–0.67). 我们没有直接验证这个假说,应力测试使用扰动投影的单图.

blocks.en: 1. Claims Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The abstract and introduction state the main contributions of V-Lumen , and the experimental sections evaluate the claimed benefits across frozen-backbone, LoRA-based, and MoE-based settings. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper. 2. Limitations Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The paper discusses its limitations in Appendix A , including that offloading the memory is a design property we do not measure. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations. 3. Theory assumptions and proofs Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof? Answer: [No] Justification: The paper does not present formal theoretical results or theorem-proof claims. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results. • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced. • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition. • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material. • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced. 4. Experimental result reproducibility Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The paper describes the model architecture, training datasets, evaluation protocol, baselines, training objective, and key hyperparameters needed to reproduce the main experimental results. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results. 5. Open access to data and code Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The paper uses public datasets and describes the experimental protocol. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc. • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why. • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable). • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted. 6. Experimental setting/details Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The paper specifies the backbone model, training stages, data mixtures, evaluation splits, baselines, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, precision, and key implementation details in the main text and appendix. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them. • The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental material. 7. Experiment statistical significance Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Main results, zero-shot results, the second-backbone results, and the ablations report mean ± \pm standard deviation over three seeds; the layer-wise logit-lens analysis reports mean ± \pm standard deviation over three seeds. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text. 8. Experiments compute resources Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Appendix E.1 reports the GPU type and number used for training, the wall-clock time of each training configuration and of evaluation, and the total compute used for the reported experiments; training schedules and batch sizes are given in Appendix E.2 , and latency and GPU memory measurements, including the hardware used, are reported in Appendix H.1 . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster, or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage. • The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute. • The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that didn’t make it into the paper). 9. Code of ethics Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines ? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The work uses public benchmarks and pretrained models for methodological research, and we have reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and believe the research conforms to it. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. • If the authors answer [No] , they should explain the special circumstances that require a deviation from the Code of Ethics. • The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consideration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction). 10. Broader impacts Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The paper discusses that improving VLM reasoning can benefit document, chart, and multimodal understanding applications, while also acknowledging potential risks from more capable VLMs such as incorrect or overconfident predictions in downstream use. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML). 11. Safeguards Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pre-trained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not introduce or release a new high-risk pretrained generative model, scraped dataset, or deployment system requiring additional release safeguards. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper poses no such risks. • Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing safety filters. • Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images. • We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best faith effort. 12. Licenses for existing assets Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We cite the original papers for all pretrained models, datasets, and benchmarks, and use them in accordance with their respective licenses and terms of use. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset. • For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided. • If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators. 13. New assets Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not currently release a new dataset, benchmark, or model checkpoint as a new public asset. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets. • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc. • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used. • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file. 14. Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not involve new crowdsourcing experiments or research with human subjects. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector. 15. Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not involve human-subject studies, so IRB or equivalent approval is not applicable. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper. • We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution. • For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review. 16. Declaration of LLM usage Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required. Answer: [N/A] Justification: The core method does not use LLMs as an important, original, or non-standard component. The pretrained vision-language backbones (Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct and InternVL3.5-2B) are the standard models that V-Lumen augments and are described in the paper. No LLM is used to generate or annotate training data, and evaluation uses rule-based accuracy without LLM-based judging. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the core method development in this research does not involve LLMs as any important, original, or non-standard components. • Please refer to our LLM policy in the NeurIPS handbook for what should or should not be described.
blocks.zh: 一、导 言 索赔问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 抽象和引言陈述了V-Lumen的主要贡献,实验部分评价了冻结后骨、基于LORA和基于教育部的设置中声称的好处。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指摘要和导言不包括文件中提出的要求。 抽象和(或)导言应明确说明所提出的要求,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 审议人员不会很好地看待对这一问题的[否]或[无]答复。 所提出的主张应与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果可以归纳到其他场合。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。 2. 限制问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 文件在附录A中讨论了其局限性,包括卸载内存是我们不计量的设计属性. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指文件没有限制,而答案[否]是指文件有限制,但在文件中没有讨论。 鼓励作者在论文中另辟一个“限制”部分。 文件应说明任何强有力的假设,以及这些假设遭到违反(例如,独立性假设、无噪声设置、模型精确度、不对称近似只在当地持有)的结果如何有力。 作者应思考这些假设在实践中可能如何遭到违反,其影响如何。 作者应反思所提出主张的范围,例如,如果这种办法只在几个数据集或几个运行中测试。 一般来说,经验性结果往往取决于隐含的假设,这些假设应当加以阐述。 作者应反思影响该办法执行的因素。 例如,一个面部识别算法在图像分辨率低或图像在低光照下拍摄时可能表现不佳. 或语音对文本系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线讲座提供闭门字幕,因为它无法处理技术术语。 作者应讨论拟议算法的计算效率,以及它们如何用数据集大小来衡量。 如果适用,作者应讨论他们处理隐私和公平问题的办法可能存在的局限性。 虽然作者可能担心审查人员会以完全诚实的限度作为拒绝的理由,但更糟糕的结果可能是审查人员发现文件中不承认的限制。 作者应运用最佳判断,承认有利于透明度的个别行动在制定维护社会完整性的规范方面发挥着重要作用。 将特别指示审查人员不要惩罚在限制方面的诚实。 3. 理论假设和证明 问题: 对于每一项理论结果,论文是否提供了一整套假设和完整的(和正确的)证明? 答复:理由: 本文不提出正式的理论结果或防理主张. 准则: • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括理论结果. • 支助 所有论文中的定理,公式和证明,都应该编号,相互参照. • 支助 所有假设都应在任何定理的说明中明确说明或提及。 证据可以出现在主要论文或补充材料中,但如果在补充材料中出现,则鼓励作者提供简短的证据草图以提供直觉. • 反之,文件核心中提供的任何非正式证据都应辅以附录或补充材料中提供的正式证据。 • 应适当参考证据所依据的定理和莱玛。 4. 实验结果可复制 问题: 文件是否充分披露复制文件主要实验结果所需的所有信息,以影响文件的主要主张和/或结论(无论是否提供代码和数据)? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 文件介绍了复制主要实验结果所需的模型架构、培训数据集、评价协议、基线、培训目标以及关键超参数。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果论文包括实验,审查人员将不会很好地看待对这一问题的回答: 使文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或可核查而采取的步骤。 • 根据贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一个具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人有可能用同样的数据集复制这个模型,或者提供对模型的访问. 总论中. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一点的好方法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. • 支助 虽然NeurIPS并不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交材料都为可复制性提供某种合理的途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当明确说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范结构,文件应清楚、全面地描述这种结构。 (c) 如果贡献是一个新的模型(例如大语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(例如,有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示). (d) 我们认识到,在某些情况下,可复制性可能很困难,在这种情况下,欢迎作者描述它们为可复制性规定的具体方式。 对于封闭源代码模型,可能以某种方式(如注册用户)限制对模型的获取,但其他研究者应该有一定途径复制或验证结果. 5. 开放存取数据和代码问题: 文件是否提供了开放的数据和代码,并有足够的指示,如补充材料所述,忠实地复制主要的实验结果? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 论文使用公共数据集并描述了实验协议. · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括需要代码的实验。 详情请见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmission Policy)。 虽然我们鼓励发布代码和数据,但我们理解这也许是不可能的,因此[否]是一个可以接受的答案. 不能仅仅因为没有包含代码而拒绝文件,除非这是贡献的核心(例如,对于一个新的开源基准). • 支助 指示应包含复制结果所需的准确命令和环境。 详情见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 作者应提供关于数据存取和准备的说明,包括如何获取原始数据、预先处理的数据、中间数据以及生成的数据等。 作者应提供脚本,复制所有实验结果,用于新的拟议方法和基线。 如果只有一组实验可以复制,它们应该说明哪些实验从脚本中删除,以及为什么。 在提交来文时,为保留匿名性,提交人应公布匿名版本(如适用)。 • 建议在补充材料中提供尽可能多的信息(附于文件),但允许将URL纳入数据和代码。 6. 实验设置/细节问题: 文件是否具体说明了解结果所需的所有培训和测试细节(如数据分割、超参数、如何选择、优化者的类型)? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 文件在正文和附录中具体规定了骨干模型,培训阶段,数据混合物,评价划分,基线,优化者,学习率时间表,精度,以及关键实施细节. · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 实验环境应在文件核心中详细介绍,以便了解结果,使之合理。 详细情况可通过附录中的代码或补充材料提供。 7. 实验统计意义 问题: 纸质报告错误是否含有适当和正确定义的信息或关于实验统计意义的其他适当信息? 答复:[是] 说明:主要结果,0射出结果,第二后骨结果,和擦伤报告表示±\pm标准差大于3个种子;分层对数-连数分析报告表示±\pm标准差大于3个种子. · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果结果附有错误栏、信任间隔或统计意义测试,至少对于支持论文主要主张的实验,作者应回答[是]。 应明确说明错误条所捕获的变异因素(例如,列车/测试拆分、初始化、随机绘制某些参数,或在特定实验条件下的总体运行)。 计算错误栏的方法应当加以解释(封闭的表单公式、调用库函数、靴子陷阱等) • 应给出假设(例如,通常分布错误)。 应明确误差栏是标准偏差还是平均值的标准误差. ^ 报告1-西格玛错误栏是正常的,但应该说明这一点。 如果错误的正常性假设没有得到核实,提交人最好报告2-西格玛错误栏,而不是说他们有96%的CI。 • 支助 对于不对称分布,作者应注意不要在表格或数字对称误差栏中显示会产生超出范围的结果(如负误差率). • 支助 如果在表格或图中报告错误栏,作者应在文字中解释它们是如何计算的,并在文字中参考相应的数字或表格。 8. 实验计算资源 问题:对于每个实验,论文是否提供了复制实验所需的计算机资源(计算工人类型,内存,执行时间)的充分信息? 答复:[是]说明:附录E.1报告培训所用的GPU类型和数量,每次培训配置和评价的时钟时间,以及报告实验所用的总计算;培训时间表和批量尺寸载于附录E.2;延迟和GPU内存测量,包括所使用的硬件,载于附录H.1。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 纸张应说明计算工人的CPU或GPU、内部集群或云提供商的类型,包括相关的内存和存储。 文件应提供每次试验所需的计算数额,并估计计算总额。 论文应披露完整的研究项目是否比论文中报告的实验需要更多的计算(例如初步或失败的实验,这些实验没有把它写进论文中). 9. 道德守则问题:文件中进行的研究是否在各个方面都符合《新IPS道德守则》(https://neurips.cc/public/Ethics Guidelines)? 答复:[是]理由: 这项工作采用公共基准和经过预先培训的方法研究模式,我们审查了《新IPS道德守则》,并认为研究符合该守则。 • 答案[N/A]意味着作者没有审查《新IPS道德守则》。 如果作者回答[否],他们应该解释需要偏离道德守则的特殊情况。 提交人应确保匿名(例如,如果由于其管辖范围内的法律或条例而得到特别考虑)。 10. 更广泛的影响问题:本文件是否讨论所开展工作的潜在积极社会影响和消极社会影响? blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制?

blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.zh: 理由说明: 文件在附录A中讨论了其局限性,包括卸载内存是我们不计量的设计属性.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指文件没有限制,而答案[否]是指文件有限制,但在文件中没有讨论。 鼓励作者在论文中另辟一个“限制”部分。 文件应说明任何强有力的假设,以及这些假设遭到违反(例如,独立性假设、无噪声设置、模型精确度、不对称近似只在当地持有)的结果如何有力。 作者应思考这些假设在实践中可能如何遭到违反,其影响如何。 作者应反思所提出主张的范围,例如,如果这种办法只在几个数据集或几个运行中测试。 一般来说,经验性结果往往取决于隐含的假设,这些假设应当加以阐述。 作者应反思影响该办法执行的因素。 例如,一个面部识别算法在图像分辨率低或图像在低光照下拍摄时可能表现不佳. 或语音对文本系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线讲座提供闭门字幕,因为它无法处理技术术语。 作者应讨论拟议算法的计算效率,以及它们如何用数据集大小来衡量。 如果适用,作者应讨论他们处理隐私和公平问题的办法可能存在的局限性。 虽然作者可能担心审查人员会以完全诚实的限度作为拒绝的理由,但更糟糕的结果可能是审查人员发现文件中不承认的限制。 作者应运用最佳判断,承认有利于透明度的个别行动在制定维护社会完整性的规范方面发挥着重要作用。 将特别指示审查人员不要惩罚在限制方面的诚实。

For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML).

blocks.en: Declaration of LLM usage
blocks.zh: 声明LLM的使用

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required.
blocks.zh: 问题: 论文是否描述了LLMs的使用,如果它是本研究核心方法的重要、原始或非标准组成部分? 请注意,如果LLM只用于写作,编辑或格式化目的,且不影响研究的核心方法,科学严谨性或独创性,则不需要声明.

blocks.en: Answer: [N/A]
blocks.zh: 答复:[不详]

blocks.en: Justification: The core method does not use LLMs as an important, original, or non-standard component. The pretrained vision-language backbones (Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct and InternVL3.5-2B) are the standard models that V-Lumen augments and are described in the paper. No LLM is used to generate or annotate training data, and evaluation uses rule-based accuracy without LLM-based judging.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 核心方法不使用LLMs作为重要,原始,或非标准成分. 预先训练的视觉语言骨干(Quen3-VL-2B-Instruct和InternVL3.5-2B)是V-Lumen增强的标准模型,并在论文中描述. 没有使用LLM来生成或注释培训数据,评价使用基于规则的准确性而不使用LLM的判断.
